annotation.title_clean: Chair's summary – Second 2025 session of the GGE on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (CCW/GGE.1/2025/WP.9)
annotation.title_en: Chair's summary – Second 2025 session of the GGE on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (CCW/GGE.1/2025/WP.9)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Chair of the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (Robert in den Bosch, Netherlands), United Nations
annotation.venue: United Nations Office at Geneva – CCW
named_instruments_referenced: Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions
annotation.summary_en: This is the Chair's summary of the second 2025 session (1–5 September) of the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS). It records how delegations discussed the five boxes of the rolling text: how LAWS are characterised, how international humanitarian law (IHL) applies, prohibitions and regulations, legal reviews, and accountability. It also notes where views still diverge on context-appropriate human judgement and control.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposed characterisation of LAWS: a functionally integrated combination of weapons and technological components that can identify, select and engage targets without human operator intervention
Two-tier approach of prohibitions and regulations: LAWS incapable of being used in compliance with IHL are prohibited
Context-appropriate human judgement and control is required, including limits on targets, duration, geographical scope and real-time machine learning
States should conduct legal reviews, rigorous testing and mitigation of AI bias and automation bias across the LAWS lifecycle
Responsibility and accountability cannot be transferred to machines; States must ensure individual accountability and incident investigation
